summary: PickPath auto-picker prefers Fleet over Hermes for ClassOwnerAPI, gated by a fail-closed dispatch-readiness predicate; Hermes is the fallback when Fleet is not provably ready or on explicit --via=hermes.
reason: Fleet handles all signed commands reliably from anywhere, but auto-ready must be fail-closed: signing key resolvable, tesla-control on PATH, and credentials that provably authenticate (JWT with future exp, recorded future expiry, or a refresh grant whose own preconditions are met - refresh token plus resolvable client ID). A nonempty token string is never evidence - opaque, malformed, missing-exp, expired, or unmintable tokens leave fleetReady=false so via=auto can use a running Hermes relay instead of failing Fleet auth mid-dispatch. Dispatch honors the same contract: a refresh-token-only config mints its first access token before dispatch rather than erroring not-configured. Explicit --via=fleet always attempts Fleet and lets dispatch surface specific errors.
validated_outcome: Valid-token+key+binary -> Fleet; expired-JWT-env-var+no-refresh+hermesRunning -> Hermes fallback; --via=fleet always tries Fleet
